    API reference¶

    Automatic EDA¶

    Explore tabular data without a response variable. See Automatic exploratory data analysis for examples.

    eda.auto_eda

    Explore tabular data and return an EDA report.

    eda.EDAReport

    Store the tables and PNG plots from auto_eda().

    Distributions¶

    This section contains statistical functions for various distributions for a wide range of purposes.

    General Functions¶

    This section includes approximations about the normal distribution, as well as calculations for the Poisson-binomial distribution.

    dwrap supports the normal, exponential, Weibull, lognormal, and gamma distributions. Each supports pdf, cdf, sf, inv-cdf, left-truncated-cdf, and left-truncated-inv-cdf. Append the lower cutoff to the distribution parameters for a truncated operation.

    The two log options control separate scales:

    Quantile input and output options¶

    log_p

    log

    Input

    Output

    False

    False

    Probability

    Quantile

    True

    False

    Log probability

    Quantile

    False

    True

    Probability

    Log quantile

    True

    True

    Log probability

    Log quantile

    log=True keeps its existing meaning: return the log of the output. For quantiles, use log_p=True to accept log probabilities, as in R’s qnorm(..., log.p=TRUE). The same options apply to truncated quantiles. Logged quantiles are finite only for positive quantiles. Zero produces negative infinity, and a negative quantile produces NaN.

    import numpy as np
from tsdst.distributions import dwrap

p = np.array([0.75, 0.975])
q = dwrap(p, [0, 1], "inv-cdf", "normal")
q_from_log_p = dwrap(np.log(p), [0, 1], "inv-cdf", "normal", log_p=True)
log_q = dwrap(p, [0, 1], "inv-cdf", "normal", log=True)
log_q_from_log_p = dwrap(
    np.log(p), [0, 1], "inv-cdf", "normal", log=True, log_p=True
)

    For densities, log=True returns log densities. Sum these values for the log likelihood of independent observations. Negate the sum for the negative log likelihood:

    observations = np.array([-1.0, 0.0, 1.0])
nll = -dwrap(observations, [0, 1], "pdf", "normal", log=True).sum()

    log_p is an input option for quantiles only. Use log=True for log outputs from pdf, cdf, sf, and left-truncated-cdf.

    Likelihood Functions¶

    These common likelihood functions are presented in two formats, one that is the simple likelihood definition (usable for any data), and one that assumes your data is part of a GLM or similar model.

    distributions.exponential_mle

    Maximum Likelihood Estimate of an exponential distribution (with an option for right-censoring).

    distributions.likelihood_bernoulli

    The likelihood for a binary output or bernoulli model.

    distributions.likelihood_gaussian

    The likelihood for a normal(ish) output or gaussian model.

    distributions.likelihood_poisson

    The likelihood for a count output or poisson model.

    distributions.glm_likelihood_bernoulli

    The likelihood for a logistic regression or bernoulli model with a penalty term (can accept any norm, default is 1 for L1).

    distributions.glm_likelihood_gaussian

    The likelihood for a gaussian regression model with a penalty term (can accept any norm, default is 1 for L1).

    distributions.glm_likelihood_poisson

    The likelihood for a poisson regression model with a penalty term (can accept any norm, default is 1 for L1).

    Posterior Functions¶

    These functions are mainly for Bayesian Inference, and for use with the MCMC module.

    distributions.exp_gamma

    Posterior distribution for an exponential likelihood with a gamma prior.

    distributions.NHPP_posterior

    The posterior density of the non-homogenous Poisson distribution with a power-law process.

    distributions.pois_gamma

    Posterior density for the Poisson distribution (assuming gamma prior).

    distributions.pois_gamma_ada

    Posterior density for the Poisson distribution (assuming gamma prior), learns the gamma shape/scale as part of mcmc.

    distributions.pois_uniform

    Posterior density for the Poisson distribution (assuming uniform prior).

    distributions.posterior_logreg_lasso

    Evaluate the binary logistic posterior with Laplace coefficient priors.

    distributions.ap_logreg_lasso

    Evaluate the binary logistic posterior with a learned Laplace prior scale.

    distributions.posterior_poisson_lasso

    Evaluate the Poisson posterior with normal coefficient priors.

    distributions.posterior_poisson_lasso_od

    Evaluate the generalized Poisson posterior with fixed-scale Laplace priors.

    distributions.ap_poisson_lasso_od

    Evaluate the generalized Poisson posterior with a learned normal-prior scale.

    distributions.weibull_gamma

    The posterior density for a weibull distribution with a gamma prior.

    distributions.weibull_regression_post

    Evaluate the posterior for covariate-dependent Weibull shape and a shared scale.

    Estimators¶

    Bayesian Estimators¶

    Bayesian Estimators using MCMC to calculate model parameters and associated errors.

    BayesPoissonRegressor.predict returns the conditional count mean, exp(intercept + X @ coefficients), with or without overdispersion. For the generalized Poisson likelihood, theta = mean * (1 - delta) and the conditional variance is mean / (1 - delta)**2. Predictions use the coefficient summary selected by param_summary. They do not average count means over all posterior draws.

    The adaptive overdispersion likelihood used with C=None now uses this same mean parameterization. Refit models trained with that branch.

    BayesWeibullRegressor keeps covariate-dependent shape and one shared sampled scale. predict_shape exposes shape, predict returns the mean, and predict_variance returns the Weibull variance. fit and likelihood scoring accept right-censoring indicators through status. The over_dispersion argument is retained but unused for this distribution.

    Weibull score defaults to R2. scorer="log_likelihood" returns the weighted mean log density or log survival contribution. scorer="D2" compares sums of Weibull survival-deviance residuals against a fitted null Weibull model. This descriptive D2 is not a GLM likelihood-ratio test. The Pearson residuals use the actual Weibull variance; their empirical inflation estimate is a diagnostic, not a separate distribution parameter.

    Generalized Poisson fitting uses 0 <= delta < 1 for overdispersion. Unexpected NaN or positive-infinite posterior values raise an error. Negative infinity remains a valid rejection of a proposal outside posterior support.

    estimators.BayesLogRegClassifier

    A Logistic Regression Classifier that uses MCMC to evaluate the parameters.

    estimators.BayesPoissonRegressor

    A Poisson Regressor that uses MCMC to evaluate the parameters.

    estimators.BayesWeibullRegressor

    A Weibull Regressor that uses MCMC to evaluate the parameters.

    Regularized regression uncertainty¶

    GenerateRegCov, RegressionSE, and modeling.predict accept covariance="sampling" or covariance="curvature". Sampling is the default. With information matrix S and L2 penalty matrix P, set A=S+lamda*P. Sampling covariance uses A^-1 S A^-1; curvature uses A^-1. Linear regression multiplies the matrix by an OLS noise-variance estimate. Logistic regression uses its fitted Bernoulli information matrix and unit dispersion.

    A separately fitted intercept is unpenalized by default. Set penalize_intercept=True to include it in the penalty. The supplied lamda must match the fitted model’s effective L2 penalty. These options apply to the standard-error helpers, not the Bayesian posterior priors.

    OLS intervals use Student t critical values. Logistic Wald intervals use normal critical values. Intervals for penalized fits are approximations: sampling covariance describes the shrunken estimator’s variation and does not remove shrinkage bias. Curvature intervals use a local Gaussian-prior interpretation with an estimated noise scale when needed.
